No validation is performed on this substring to check if it is a valid float representation. Therefore, if the substring is not a parsable float (e.g., empty string, non-numeric characters, multiple decimal points, etc.), `Float.parseFloat(s)` will throw a NumberFormatException. This exception is not avoided by any prior checks or validations in the code.

Thus, the NullPointerException thrown by `parseFloat` is avoided (due to the prior null-risking operation), but the NumberFormatException is not avoided.
